Article Title: ‘He got greedy’: Ex-India captain's blunt take on Arshdeep Singh after four-wicket haul
Article Text:
India bowler Arshdeep Singh celebrates with teammate Virat Kohli (AP/PTI)

Jadeja impressed with Anshul Kamboj

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India cricketer Ajay Jadeja has praised Arshdeep Singh's overall performance in India's five-wicket victory over New Zealand in the first ODI in Auckland, but believes the left-arm pacer could have avoided an expensive finish to his spell.India began their five-match ODI series with a comfortable win at Eden Park on Wednesday, November 4. In a rain-interrupted contest reduced to 32 overs per side, New Zealand were bowled out for 185 before India chased down the revised target of 143 in just 22.4 overs. Virat Kohli led the chase with a fluent 74, while Shubman Gill contributed 37 as the duo stitched together a 113-run partnership. India eventually crossed the finish line with five wickets to spare and 56 deliveries remaining.With the ball, Arshdeep was India's leading wicket-taker, claiming four wickets in his 10 overs. However, his figures of 4/70 were inflated by an expensive final over in which New Zealand tailender Blair Tickner struck him for three sixes, taking 23 runs off the over.Assessing the pacer's performance, Jadeja felt Arshdeep had been impressive for most of his spell but allowed the opportunity to complete a five-wicket haul to influence his bowling towards the end."I would call him slightly greedy. He himself said that as well. If you remove his last over, he had dismissed four batters before that and had given 40-odd runs. He got slightly greedy for the fifth wicket in the last over," Jadeja said on Sony Sports Network.Arshdeep had himself admitted after the match that the fifth wicket would have been his favourite, indicating that he was keen to complete a five-wicket haul. Despite missing out on the milestone, his four-wicket effort placed him in an exclusive group of Indian fast bowlers to achieve the feat in an ODI in New Zealand, alongside Javagal Srinath and Mohammed Shami.Jadeja, however, stressed that the expensive final over should not overshadow what Arshdeep brings to India's bowling combination. He pointed to the value of having a left-arm fast bowler in an attack that already features Jasprit Bumrah, adding that the competition for places would only benefit the team."It happens. It's natural, but Arshdeep Singh is showing that he can play in ODIs as well, which I believe is a very good thing when a left-arm seamer gets added to this attack with (Jasprit) Bumrah. The competition has increased a lot, which is very good for India," Jadeja elaborated.Jadeja also reserved praise for Anshul Kamboj, who delivered an economical spell of 2/22 from his 10 overs and walked away with the Player of the Match award.The former India batter acknowledged that Kamboj had faced questions over his bowling during his Test debut against England in 2025, particularly regarding his pace and tendency to bowl no-balls. However, he felt the youngster had shown considerable improvement in Auckland.Jadeja also suggested that Kamboj's workload before the England assignment could have contributed to his struggles, pointing out that fatigue can affect a bowler's execution. His performance against New Zealand, according to Jadeja, reflected better pace, consistency and accuracy."He bowled extremely well. The vision everyone had was that he didn't have pace when he played in England and was bowling a lot of no-balls. I think he had come after playing a lot of cricket then. So a guy also gets tired. It's not that easy. Then he was playing for the first time, but the consistency and the slight increase in his pace he showed today (Wednesday), if we talk about the accuracy amongst the four bowlers, it's Anshul Kamboj," Jadeja added.
Article Summary: India beat New Zealand by five wickets in the first ODI in Auckland. Ajay Jadeja praised Arshdeep Singh's performance, but said he could have avoided expensive final over. Jadeja also praised Anshul Kamboj's bowling, saying he had shown improvement.

Ahlawat managed just a solitary run in two matches before Pant went on to build a distinguished career.On Wednesday, Ahlawat scored his maiden first-class century, counter-attacking for Services to jeopardise Delhi’s chances of registering their first outright win of the season.The pitch at the Air Force ground in Palam hasn’t allowed fluent scoring over the three days of the match. Article Title: ‘Everybody can play on turf’: Dutch Olympic champion explains where India are falling behind
Article Text:
Floris Jan Bovelander

Mohali:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Netherlands hockey star Floris jan Bovelander believes India’s vast talent pool can only translate into sustained global success if the country improves access to artificial turf pitches and strengthens grassroots development programmes.In Punjab for the Asian Champions Trophy, Bovelander, who has been involved in hockey development projects in India for more than a decade, said the biggest difference between hockey powers such as the Netherlands and India remained infrastructure at the grassroots level.“We have more than a thousand turf pitches in the Netherlands and all kids start on turf pitches,” Bovelander said. “The techniques and tactics of modern hockey are easier to learn when you play on turf from a young age.”While India possesses a far larger playing base, he noted that many pitches remain concentrated in stadiums and elite centres, limiting access for young players.“You have pitches, but sometimes you’re not allowed to play on them because they’re in stadiums. In the Netherlands, everybody can play on the turf pitches. That’s important for development,” said the two-time Olympic gold medallist.Bovelander, who helped establish the Naval Tata Hockey Academy in Jharkhand and remains involved in community-based programmes through the Bovelander Foundation, stressed that infrastructure alone was not enough.“There is often a lot of focus on high performance, but high-performance hockey benefits from strong grassroots programmes,” he added. “You need festivals, school competitions, youth leagues and good coaching. Elite players inspire young children, but you also need a strong base underneath.”As for the Indian men’s team, Bovelander said it had developed into one of the world’s most difficult sides to beat, citing back-to-back Olympic bronze medals as evidence of its progress. However, he admitted India had occasionally fallen short in key moments at major tournaments.“They are one of the top teams in the world. Maybe they are missing a little bit in the key moments, but they are always there,” he said. “If things go their way at one of the next major tournaments, they can win.”Bovelander also called for a healthy balance between experienced players and emerging talent, saying national teams should avoid relying on reputation alone.“Players should be in the team because of their performances, not because of their history,” he said. “Young players must keep pushing the experienced ones.”India’s 2016 Junior World Cup-winning generation had gone on to form the backbone of the senior side, he noted, but the challenge now was ensuring the next crop of youngsters was given similar opportunities.As far as his discussions with Punjab’s administration is concerned, Bovelander said he hoped to explore ways of contributing to coaching and grassroots initiatives, adding that expanding access to playing facilities would be among the issues he would raise with policymakers.
Article Summary: Former Netherlands hockey star Floris jan Bovelander believes India’s vast talent pool can only translate into sustained global success if the country improves access to artificial turf pitches. He has been involved in hockey development projects in India for more than a decade.

Article Title: Kylian Mbappe creates Champions League history, joins Lionel Messi in elite list
Article Text:
Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe (AP Photo)

Mbappe milestone as Real Madrid stage comeback against AEK Athens

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe added another milestone to his impressive UEFA Champions League career on Wednesday, becoming the second-fastest player to register 100 goal contributions in the competition's history.The French superstar reached the landmark during Real Madrid's clash against AEK Athens, finding the net in the 78th minute to take his combined tally of goals and assists to 100. Mbappe has now recorded 74 goals and 26 assists in 102 Champions League appearances.Only Lionel Messi reached the milestone quicker, taking 101 matches to register 100 goal contributions. The Argentina great achieved the feat while representing Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) before moving to Major League Soccer (MLS), where he currently plays for Inter Miami.Cristiano Ronaldo remains at the top of the all-time Champions League goal contributions chart with 182, comprising 140 goals and 42 assists.The record-breaking moment came during an eventful encounter in Athens, where Real Madrid had to fight back after falling behind twice before eventually securing a 3-2 victory.AEK Athens made an early breakthrough through Aboubakary Koita, who opened the scoring in the 12th minute following an assist from Luka Jovic.Real Madrid thought they had found an equaliser when Vinicius Jr 's cross ended up in the net following a touch from Jude Bellingham. However, the goal was ruled out because the English midfielder was adjudged to be offside.Bellingham made up for the disallowed effort just three minutes later, producing an excellent backheel finish in the 32nd minute to bring Madrid back into the contest, as reported by Goal.com.Mbappe also had an opportunity to create danger when he picked out an unmarked Marc Cucurella, but the latter failed to make the most of the chance with his weaker foot.The hosts regained the advantage in the 75th minute, with Koita turning provider this time by setting up Stavro Pilo, who put AEK Athens on the verge of a memorable victory.However, Madrid responded almost immediately. Denzel Dumfries delivered a cross that Mbappe converted in the 78th minute, restoring parity while simultaneously bringing up his 100th Champions League goal contribution.With the match heading towards its conclusion, Federico Valverde stepped up with a stunning strike, finding the top corner to complete Madrid's comeback and seal a dramatic 3-2 win.The victory ensured that Mbappe's personal milestone was accompanied by another important result for Real Madrid in Europe.
Article Summary: Kylian Mbappe becomes second-fastest player to register 100 Champions League goal contributions. The French forward reached the landmark during Real Madrid's 3-2 win against AEK Athens on Wednesday. Only Lionel Messi reached the milestone quicker, taking 101 matches to do so.

Article Title: How NBA is looking to turn India into a billion-dollar basketball market
Article Text:
Left to right: Rajah Chaudhry (NBA's Head of Strategy, Asia Pacific), Sunny Malik (Country Head, NBA India), DeMarcus Cousins and Isiah Thomas. (Image: LinkedIn)

New Delhi:

FIRST NBA STORE IN INDIA TO OPEN IN 2027 THROUGH EXPANDED MERCHANDISING PARTNERSHIP WITH SUDITI.

Tissot are the official timing partner of the NBA. (Instagram)

Crowd at the BUDX NBA House in New Delhi, India. (Instagram)

For a league that has spent decades turning basketball players into global icons and team jerseys into fashion statements, the NBA 's ambitions in India were never going to be restricted to television screens. The challenge, however, is turning that appeal into a sustainable business.India, with its young population, expanding digital audience and growing appetite for global sports and entertainment, represents a significant long-term opportunity for the league. But the NBA is conscious that building a presence in a cricket-dominated market requires more than securing a broadcaster and hoping fans tune in to watch games played thousands of kilometres and many timezones away.It is looking to create multiple entry points for consumers, with basketball, fashion, music, entertainment and retail forming parts of a larger commercial strategy.The latest step in that direction is the expansion of its merchandising partnership with Indian apparel company Suditi. Having worked together since 2018, the two have extended their association, with Suditi taking over the operation of NBAStore.in in October 2026.The expanded portfolio includes casual shirts and lifestyle footwear, alongside jerseys, T-shirts, jackets, sweatshirts, headwear and accessories.More significantly, the partnership will see the NBA open its first physical store in India in 2027. It is an important development for a league looking to take its relationship with fans beyond digital engagement and into everyday consumption.The idea is to make NBA merchandise a lifestyle proposition rather than limit it to conventional sports apparel. Its teams, players and iconic jerseys already have recognition beyond basketball-following circles. Just look at numerous LA Lakers, Chicago Bulls, Michael Jordan, Steph Curry, LeBron James knockoffs that get sold in the local markets. The opportunity lies in converting that cultural appeal into official merchandise sales.Long-term commercial partnerships are another important part of the NBA's business model. Swiss watchmaker Tissot, which has been associated with the league for a decade, is an example of how these relationships can evolve beyond brand visibility."Our partnerships are built on shared values, a common vision and a commitment to evolving together. The decade-long NBA association exemplifies this, with both brands continually innovating to enhance fan experience, most recently through a redesigned shot clock now adopted across the WNBA," Tissot CEO Sylvain Dolla told TimesofIndia.com.Dolla added that the same approach extended to the brand's associations across basketball, cycling and motorsport, where it works with Swiss Timing to develop sport-specific solutions. "Our objective is to contribute to each sport's growth through long-term collaboration and innovation," he added.But retail and partnerships are only part of the equation.The NBA has spent considerable time experimenting with how Indian audiences consume its product. Its broadcast journey has included a decade-long association with Sony, followed by partnerships with MTV and digital platforms. It also explored making 100 games available live on YouTube, while its three-year association with Prasar Bharati took basketball content to DD Sports and a wider free-to-air audience.The reasoning was straightforward: live games alone cannot drive growth in a market where matches are played at inconvenient hours for Indian viewers."You can't just focus on broadcast and say, 'please watch my game.' You have to do other things around the sport," said Rajah Chaudhry, NBA's Asia-Pacific head of strategy, during an interaction with TimesofIndia.com in June."The objective is not to get cocooned into just one way of saying that live games are the way to be. We want to try different ways because people like to consume games in different ways in the country. That's our objective," added Sunny Malik, NBA India's Country Head.For the 2026-27 season, NBA games are available live in India on Prime Video and NBA League Pass. The challenge is to ensure that audiences remain connected to the league even when they are not watching live action.That is where digital content assumes importance. The NBA's Indian social media platforms have accumulated more than eight million followers, generating over 1.8 billion impressions and 1.35 billion video views. Highlights, short-form clips, player stories and locally produced content allow the league to remain part of the conversation throughout the year.Its approach to fan engagement also extends beyond the screen.BUDX NBA House, which moved from Mumbai to New Delhi in May this year, brings basketball together with music, fashion, celebrity appearances and entertainment. The format is particularly relevant in India, where the NBA's cultural appeal can reach audiences who may not necessarily follow the sport closely.The initiative has also found relevance beyond India, with elements of the experience informing the league's approach in other Asia-Pacific markets.There is, however, a distinction between building awareness and building a business. Social media numbers and event attendance offer encouraging signs, but converting occasional engagement into regular viewership, merchandise sales and long-term commercial partnerships remains the bigger test.Cricket continues to command the country's sporting attention, sponsorship money and broadcast market. The NBA also has to contend with a time-zone disadvantage and the challenge of developing a sizeable paying audience for a sport that still occupies a relatively small space in India's domestic sporting landscape.The league's India strategy, therefore, is built around connecting several businesses rather than relying on one. Broadcast distribution creates visibility, digital content sustains engagement, live experiences build communities, while merchandise and retail offer opportunities to monetise that relationship.The pieces are gradually falling into place. The question is whether they can come together to create something bigger.For the NBA, India's opportunity is not merely about getting more people to watch basketball. It is about making the league part of their sporting, cultural and consumer lives.
Article Summary: The NBA is expanding its merchandising partnership with Indian apparel company Suditi. The partnership will see the NBA open its first physical store in India in 2027. It is an important development for a league looking to take its relationship with fans beyond digital engagement and into everyday consumption.

Article Title: BCCI backs president’s team after High Court ruling as Meghalaya side changed overnight
Article Text:
Meghalaya's internal cricket battle takes centre stage after HC ruling

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: Meghalaya’s Ranji Trophy Plate Group campaign took a dramatic turn ahead of its fourth-round match against Nagaland, with the team selected under Meghalaya Cricket Association (MCA) president James Sangma taking the field after a recent Meghalaya High Court order dated Oct 30, 2026, effectively shifted the selection process to his faction.The development came despite Meghalaya’s encouraging start to the season. The side that played the first three rounds had collected 12 points, registering one win for six points and earning three points each from two drawn matches.The team that featured in the opening three games had been selected through a process initiated by the MCA secretary Rayonald Kharkamni’s faction. However, a legal dispute between rival groups within the association led to a High Court ruling that upheld the president’s actions and set aside decisions taken by the secretary-led Apex Council.Explaining the BCCI ’s position, secretary Devajit Saikia told TOI: “The Meghalaya team which participated in the first three matches was selected by the selection committee and the process initiated by the then MCA secretary. There was a pending litigation going on for the last few months between the two groups of Meghalaya Cricket Association. One group is headed by the secretary, and the other group by the president.”On why the Board allowed the total overhaul of the side overnight, Saikia said: “BCCI has no option but to abide by the order of the honorable Meghalaya High Court which has upheld the president’s action. So, we have to allow the team selected at the initiative of the president play.”Saikia also distinguished the Meghalaya situation from the recent Arunachal Pradesh case, where BCCI stepped in to facilitate team selection after the association failed to field a side.“In Arunachal case, there was no team. There was no one at the helm of affairs in the cricket association. Therefore, nobody was selecting the team or there was no process. So as a result, BCCI had to step in to select a squad,” he said.However, the fate of players from the earlier Meghalaya team remains uncertain. Asked whether BCCI could intervene, Saikia said they would have to seek relief through the courts or the ombudsman. “If somebody feels deprived, at this stage there is an ombudsman, they can raise all their objections before the ombudsman.”Saikia maintained that BCCI would not intervene in the internal dispute, with a team now representing the state. “BCCI is happy that somebody is playing. Who’s playing that is not our concern,” said Saikia.
Article Summary: Meghalaya's Ranji Trophy Plate Group campaign took a dramatic turn ahead of its fourth-round match against Nagaland. The team that featured in the opening three games had been selected through a process initiated by the MCA secretary Rayonald Kharkamni’s faction. However, a legal dispute between rival groups within the association led to a High Court ruling that upheld the president's actions.

NEW DELHI: "Desh ke liye khelne ke liye jigra chahiye hota hai (It takes guts to play for the country)," Jayant Goyat told this reporter on the sidelines of Day 2 of the ongoing Ranji Trophy match between Delhi and Services at the Air Force Complex Ground in Palam.The conversation revolved around the challenges of bowling on a Palam pitch, where conditions are often either flat or favour spin, and how a 21-year-old fast bowler keeps his India ambition alive while operating in such conditions.On Day 3, Goyat registered his maiden five-wicket haul in his 12th first-class appearance for Services. His early breakthroughs on Wednesday helped Services fight back in the game."It is a very good feeling. It is my first fifer. The wicket is slow and flat, so I had to put in extra effort. I did that and got the results," he told reporters.It was a double delight for the six-foot-four-inch-tall pacer, who hails from Haryana's Bhiwani district. The 21-year-old, who joined the Air Force through the Agniveer scheme, has received an extension after the Union Cabinet approved an additional two-year engagement period for 75% of Agniveers. The lanky seamer, who has played all his age-group cricket for Haryana, just smiled when a handful of reporters broke the news to him.Services head coach AP Singh, a Lieutenant Colonel in the Indian Army, lauded Goyat and said he sees a lot of potential in the youngster."Absolutely, he is an exciting talent, and we are in the process of grooming him for the next level. He has age on his side, he is talented, and he is bowling very well. This was his first five-wicket haul today in a very big game. He is an exciting talent," said the coach."He bowled brilliantly today. That is what we had discussed in the team meeting. All they need to do on these wickets is bowl in good areas and not go searching for wickets. Being a youngster full of enthusiasm, there is a tendency to go for wickets. That is where you leak runs and don't even get a wicket," added Singh.Jayant's five-wicket haul was a significant step in that learning process, with the coach pointing out how the youngster had applied the lessons discussed in the team meeting."Today's five-wicket haul was a big learning experience for him. In fact, he categorically told me that what we discussed in the team meeting had worked for him. Just bowl in good areas and good lengths, and you will get wickets," said Singh.Although Bhiwani is known for producing athletes in combat sports, Goyat grew up in a cricket-loving family. His father, Dr Wazir Singh Goyat, was part of the Haryana Ranji Trophy team during Kapil Dev 's last season. Although he never got the opportunity to make his debut, Goyat Sr. never stopped his son from pursuing his dream. He is currently working as a professor of physical education at Maharaja Neempal Singh Government College in Bhiwani."My father took me to cricket. He also played Ranji Trophy for Haryana. He was a fast bowler and was part of the squad during Kapil Dev's last season," Goyat said."I played for India Under-19 last season and was on standby for the World Cup (2024). I got to know [about Services]. I knew local guys in Services. I gave a trial and got selected," he added.Goyat recollected his father's unwavering support during the time he was playing for India Under-19 and was not able to perform well."My father never pushed me to play cricket. He let me do what I wanted. I wanted to play cricket. He supported me a lot. I can't even say how much. Even when I was down a lot, he gave me a lot of moral support," he said."When I played India Under-19, I wasn't performing for three-four matches on the trot for Haryana. I said one time that I was quitting cricket. He pushed me, and then my team started performing well. Depending on his mood, he motivates me in different ways. He motivated me then by giving me my favourite food," added Goyat with a smile.Goyat, who has played all his cricket as a batting all-rounder, idolises legendary South African all-rounder Jacques Kallis and has batted in the top order. He says he is training hard to add a few yards to his bowling."My natural length is back of a length. I do look to hit the deck. I do think I can add speed. At Under-19, I bowled at 134-135 kmph. It is about the training regime to add speed. I work with the Services S&C. The main thing is about strength. It is about strengthening the lower body. The more I do strength training, the better it is," he said.Meanwhile, Services coach showered praise on Jayant's attitude, describing him as someone who brings positivity into the dressing room and does not get weighed down by setbacks."As far as I have seen, he is a jolly good fellow. He is always happy and creates a good environment in the team. He doesn't get bogged down easily. Attitude is a very big thing, and that is what we look for in players. That is how players grow and perform well at this stage."
Article Summary: Jayant Goyat is a fast bowler who plays for Services in the Ranji Trophy. The 21-year-old recorded his maiden five-wicket haul in his 12th first-class appearance for Services. The six-foot-four-inch-tall pacer hails from Haryana's Bhiwani district.

NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli added another landmark to his extraordinary ODI career on Wednesday, becoming the first batter in the history of the format to maintain an average of 50 or more in all four SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.The India batting stalwart achieved the feat during the first ODI against New Zealand at Auckland, where he produced an authoritative 74 off just 51 balls. His innings, studded with 13 fours and a six, came at a strike rate of over 145 and helped India negotiate a rain-curtailed chase with ease.Kohli's average in New Zealand stood at 49.66 before the match. His latest knock took it to 51.53, completing a unique set of 50-plus averages across the four countries. He now averages 76.38 in South Africa, 51.48 in England, 51.53 in New Zealand and 50.03 in Australia.The milestone underlines Kohli's remarkable consistency in conditions traditionally regarded as challenging for visiting batters. He has scored 993 runs in South Africa, 1,493 in England, 670 in New Zealand and 1,401 in Australia.The Auckland innings also saw Kohli move past another iconic record held by Sachin Tendulkar . He became the highest run-scorer in ODI run-chases, taking his tally to 8,741 runs and going past Tendulkar's 8,720.Kohli has accumulated those runs in 180 matches and 169 innings at an average of 66.21 and a strike rate of 95.03, with 30 centuries and 46 half-centuries.His numbers in successful chases are even more striking. The former India captain has scored 6,477 runs in 114 matches and 108 innings at an average of 89.95 and a strike rate above 98. That tally includes 25 centuries and 30 fifties, with a highest score of 183.The record further reinforces Kohli's reputation as one of the most prolific batters in ODI chases, particularly when India are pursuing a target.Kohli also drew level with Australian great Ricky Ponting for the most ODI runs against New Zealand. Both batters now have 1,971 runs against the Black Caps.Kohli has reached the mark in 37 innings at an average of 57.97 and a strike rate of 97.86, with seven centuries and 11 half-centuries. Ponting took 50 innings across 51 matches to score the same number of runs, averaging 45.83, with six centuries and 12 fifties.The India batter also became the first player to reach 13,000 ODI runs while batting at No. 3. He has scored 13,062 runs in 254 matches and 251 innings at the position, averaging 61.61. His tally includes 48 centuries and 70 half-centuries, with a best score of 183.Kohli's latest milestone comes amid an impressive run in the 50-over format. Since retiring from Test cricket, he has scored 1,002 runs in 16 ODIs at an average of 77.07, including four centuries and six half-centuries.He has also been among the leading performers in ODIs this year. In 10 matches, Kohli has accumulated 626 runs at an average of 69.55 and a strike rate of 120.61. The tally features two centuries and four fifties, with a highest score of 139 not out. Kohli's innings was among the major highlights of India's five-wicket victory in the rain-affected series opener at Auckland.After being put under pressure by India's bowlers, New Zealand were bowled out for 185. Arshdeep Singh spearheaded the attack with an impressive four-wicket haul, while Gurnoor Brar claimed three wickets for 44 runs in 9.2 overs. Anshul Kamboj chipped in with two wickets, conceding just 22 runs in his 10 overs.India were set a revised target of 143 in 32 overs under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method after rain interruptions. Kohli's brisk 74 ensured the chase remained on course, as India reached the target comfortably to take an early lead in the series.
Article Summary: Virat Kohli becomes the first batter to maintain an average of 50 or more in all four SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia. The India batting stalwart achieved the feat during the first ODI against New Zealand at Auckland. His innings, studded with 13 fours and a six, came at a strike rate of over 145 and helped India negotiate a rain-curtailed chase.

Article Title: Heartbreaking defeat! Lizelle Lee's rare wicketkeeping error denies Hobart Hurricanes a Super Over against Melbourne Renegade - Watch
Article Text:
Lee's rare wicketkeeping error costs Hobart Hurricanes (Images: X)

Over-rate penalty adds to Hurricanes' late heartbreak

Nicola Carey, Chinelle Henry power Hurricanes to 154

Hayley Matthews leads Renegades before late collapse

Melbourne Renegades pulled off a dramatic four-wicket victory over Hobart Hurricanes in the Women's Big Bash League (WBBL) on Wednesday, with a rare wicketkeeping infringement on the final delivery denying the hosts a chance to force a Super Over. Just when the Hurricanes appeared to have rescued a thrilling contest, Lizelle Lee 's positioning behind the stumps turned the game on its head, handing the Renegades a victory through a no-ball decision at Bellerive Oval.Chasing 155, the Renegades needed one run from the final delivery with scores level at 154. Deandra Dottin failed to connect with Nicola Carey 's delivery, and Lee collected the ball behind the stumps. Both teams appeared to be preparing for a Super Over, but the third umpire intervened after television replays showed that Lee had collected the ball in front of the stumps.Under Law 27.3, a wicketkeeper must remain wholly behind the striker's wicket until the ball touches the batter or their bat, passes the wicket, or the batter attempts a run. Any breach of this provision results in a no-ball being called. The decision awarded the Renegades the additional run they needed to seal a four-wicket win without a Super Over.The dramatic finish followed another crucial twist in the final over.The Hurricanes were penalised for failing to complete their 20 overs within the stipulated time and were allowed only two fielders outside the 30-yard circle for the final three deliveries.After a dot ball, Dottin edged the penultimate delivery towards the deep third boundary. With the boundary rider unavailable because of the fielding restriction, the ball raced away for four, bringing the scores level at 154.Dottin then missed the final delivery, and Lee's infringement completed a remarkable turnaround for the visitors. The Hurricanes were left stunned as the Renegades celebrated their first victory of the WBBL|12 campaign.Earlier, Hobart Hurricanes posted 154/7 in their 20 overs, with captain Nicola Carey leading the charge in her 150th WBBL appearance. Carey struck 62 off 43 deliveries, providing stability to an innings that saw the Hurricanes lose wickets at regular intervals.West Indian all-rounder Chinelle Henry added a quickfire 36 off just 18 balls to give the hosts a late boost. However, Henry later hobbled off after bowling just one over, which cost 14 runs, with a suspected hip injury.Renegades captain Sophie Molineux led the bowling attack with figures of 4/22, taking her career WBBL tally to 101 wickets. She became only the second player in the franchise's history to reach the 100-wicket milestone, after Molly Strano.In reply, Hayley Matthews kept the Renegades on course with an impressive 59 off 44 deliveries, while Courtney Webb contributed 29 off 25 balls. The pair helped the visitors build a strong platform before the Hurricanes fought back.The Renegades suffered a dramatic collapse, losing five wickets for 37 runs after reaching 101, bringing the contest back into balance. Matthews was dismissed by Heather Graham, while Molly Strano produced a superb catch-and-bowl effort to remove Molineux.With 33 runs required from the final four overs, the Renegades used the Power Surge to keep the chase alive. Despite the late setbacks, they eventually crossed the line in one of the most unusual finishes of the tournament.The victory gave the Renegades their first win of the WBBL season 12, while the Hurricanes remained without a win after three matches and at the bottom of the standings.
Article Summary: Melbourne Renegades beat Hobart Hurricanes by four wickets in Women's Big Bash League (WBBL) Late wicketkeeping infringement denies hosts chance to force a Super Over. Renegades needed one run from the final delivery with scores level at 154.

Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

From 14 medals to 114: India's remarkable rise

India's Asian Para Games record

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Smaller contingent, bigger return

Hangzhou vs Aichi-Nagoya

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Athletics powers India's medal surge

India's leading medal-winning sports in Asian Para Games 2026

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Multiple medallists underline India's depth

Paralympic progress provides the wider context

Fourth place sets a new benchmark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

Article Title: Asian Para Games bronze leaves Suhas Yathiraj hungry for gold amid IAS duties and badminton
Article Text:

Third Paralympics, one big dream: Gold at LA 2028

IAS officer by day, shuttler by night

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.
Article Summary: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. The Indian shuttler lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23- 21, 8-21, 15-21. Suhas has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024.

NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental competition concluded with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the ceremony, marking the end of a landmark campaign in which the country's para-athletes delivered historic victories, world-record performances and podium sweeps across disciplines.India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.Held in Japan for the first time, the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games brought together around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. The competition featured 18 sports, with more than 20 world records reportedly set during the seven-day event.China topped the medal table with 435 medals, including 207 gold, while hosts Japan finished second with 186 medals — 64 gold, 60 silver and 62 bronze.Uzbekistan emerged as the third-ranked nation, collecting 145 medals, including 45 gold.India's fourth-place finish was particularly significant given the size of its contingent. A total of 168 para-athletes represented the country at Aichi-Nagoya, compared with 309 at the previous edition in Hangzhou.President Droupadi Murmu congratulated the Indian contingent on its record performance, saying the achievement reflected the athletes' hard work, perseverance and self-belief.In a post on X, Murmu said the unprecedented medal haul would inspire young people to dream big, work with dedication and remain positive in the face of challenges. She also extended her congratulations to the entire Indian contingent.Para athletics was India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. Para badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze.India also won 11 medals in para swimming, seven in para table tennis, six in para archery and five in para shooting. The contingent added two medals each in para judo and para powerlifting.The closing ceremony brought together athletes, officials and dignitaries to mark the conclusion of the Games. Asian Paralympic Committee president Majid Rashed declared the event closed, highlighting the growing strength of para sport across Asia and its role in building a more inclusive society.Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also praised the athletes' determination, teamwork and sportsmanship, describing their performances as a reminder of the “profound beauty” of para sports.The Asian Para Games began in Guangzhou, China, in 2010, evolving from the Far East and South Pacific Games Federation for the Disabled. The Aichi-Nagoya edition was the fifth staging of the event, with Doha, Qatar, scheduled to host the sixth in 2030.For India, the closing ceremony marked the end of a historic campaign — one that raised the country's medal benchmark and showcased the depth and growing strength of its para-sport movement.
Article Summary: India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games. A total of 168 para-athletes represented the country at Aichi-Nagoya, compared with 309 at the previous edition in Hangzhou.

Article Title: Navdeep Singh credits SAI JLN Stadium support as India deliver record Asian Para Games medal haul

NEW DELHI: Indian para-javelin star Navdeep Singh has credited the support and training facilities at the Sports Authority of India’s (SAI) Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) Stadium in New Delhi for helping the country’s para-athletes deliver a historic performance at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games.India finished fourth in the continental competition with a record 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — its best-ever haul at the Games. Para athletics led the charge with 65 medals, including 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze.Navdeep won bronze in the men’s javelin throw F40/F41 on Friday, improving on his fourth-place finish at the 2022 edition. The Paris Paralympics gold medallist said training alongside fellow athletes at the JLN Stadium’s main track helped him prepare for the competition environment in Aichi-Nagoya.“Most of us Asian Games-bound athletes, including me, did our preparations at the JLN Stadium for the Asian Games 2026,” said Navdeep after his medal win. “This allowed us to acclimatise and get the feel. Despite the ongoing [Indian Super League] football matches, they kept the Asian Games a priority, which I felt was quite impressive, and that supported me,” he added.Navdeep also highlighted how access to the main track allowed athletes across disciplines to focus on their preparations without unnecessary delays.“Sprinters need an empty track, so they got a good chance to train inside it. I majorly train at the SAI Regional Centres [Bengaluru, Sonipat and Gandhinagar], where there is not much crowd and I don’t have to wait for other athletes to finish their throws. This all happened here at the JLN Stadium too. I could focus on my preparations rather than focusing on rotations and waiting for my turn,” Navdeep said, expressing hopes of returning to the JLN Stadium for the next season.A total of 14 para-athletics medallists from the Aichi-Nagoya Games trained at the JLN Stadium ahead of the competition. More than 50 other para-athletes also train at the facility.The athletes who trained at the facility delivered medals across track and field events. Gold medallists included Praveen Kumar in the men’s high jump T64, Sandeep Kumar in the men’s 400m T64, where he set a world record, Pranav Soorma in the men’s club throw F51, Rinku Hooda in the men’s javelin throw F46, and Simran Sharma, who won the women’s 100m and 200m T12 titles, setting Games records in both events.The silver medallists included Manjeet, Nimisha Chakkungalparambil, Varun Singh Bhati, Preeti Pal and Ajeet Singh Yadav. Bronze medallists included Sandeep Kumar in the men’s 100m T44, Sandip Sanjay Sargar in the men’s javelin combined classification event, Navdeep in the men’s javelin F40/F41 and Anubhav Choudhary in the men’s 100m T35.The medal-winning performances highlighted the contribution of the JLN Stadium’s training environment to India’s record campaign at the Asian Para Games.

Article Title: India script history with best-ever haul of 114 medals as nine golds cap golden day at Asian Para Games

NEW DELHI: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games, registering their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals, including 30 gold, after a record-breaking final-day flourish in Aichi-Nagoya on Friday.India collected nine gold medals on the day — their biggest single-day haul of the ongoing edition — with champions emerging from badminton, archery, shooting and athletics. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023.The achievement was particularly significant as India competed with a contingent of 168 athletes, nearly half the size of the squad that represented the country in Hangzhou.India remained fourth in the standings at the end of its campaign, although the final positions could change after a few remaining events on Saturday.Athletics remained India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals, 12 more than at the previous edition. On Friday, however, the spotlight was shared with a superb badminton campaign and gold-winning performances in shooting and archery. Star javelin thrower Sumit Antil led an Indian 1-2-3 finish in the men's F42-44/61-64 combined event . The reigning Paralympic and world champion threw 72.46m to defend his title, while Mahendra Gurjar took silver with 59.03m and Sandip Sanjay Sargar claimed bronze with 64.48m. Gurjar finished ahead of Sargar on Raza points, which determine rankings in combined-classification events.Pranav Soorma added another gold in the men's club throw F51, defending his title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m. Dharambir secured bronze with 27.71m.Sandeep delivered a world-record performance in the men's 400m T64, clocking 52.28 seconds for gold. India's Ajay Kumar also reached the podium, winning bronze in a Games-record time of 53.61 seconds.Haney produced another world record, throwing 60.49m to win the men's javelin F37/38 title. India also picked up silver medals through Nimisha Chakkungalparambil in the women's long jump T47 and Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46, where he clocked 4:09.65.India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar and Games debutant Naveen Sivakumar.Nitesh defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles SL3 final. He later added a silver medal in mixed doubles SL3-SU5 alongside Thulasimathi Murugesan.Naveen, meanwhile, defeated Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 to win the men's singles SL4 title. Thulasimathi enjoyed a memorable campaign of her own , combining with Manasi Joshi to win gold in women's doubles SL3-SU5. The Indian pair beat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final.The 24-year-old also secured silver in women's singles SU5 after losing 18-21, 11-21 to Yang in the final, completing a three-medal haul.Shooter Mona Agarwal added another golden chapter to India's campaign, shattering the world record to win the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 title with a score of 357.5 points.The 38-year-old had earlier won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold with a Games-record score of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara, who took silver with 249.6.Mona's latest triumph gave her a second gold of the Games and further underlined her standing among India's leading para-shooters. She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.India's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver. Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.
Article Summary: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin 1-2-3 as Pranav Soorma strikes gold again

Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep

Pranav Soorma defends club throw crown

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.The 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Competitors perform their throws from a seated position.With Antil leading a historic Indian sweep in the javelin and Soorma retaining his title, India's para-athletes delivered another memorable day in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep at the Asian Para Games. Pranav Soorma defends his title in the men's club throw F51 event. Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar complete all-Indian podium finish.

NEW DELHI: Double gold medallists Mona Agarwal and Nishad Kumar will be India's flag-bearers at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, following outstanding campaigns in shooting and para-athletics.Both athletes won two gold medals each at the continental event, with Mona producing a record-breaking performance in shooting and Nishad excelling in the high jump and long jump.Their selection as flag-bearers recognises their achievements as India prepare to bring the Games to a close.The 38-year-old Mona opened India's medal account in shooting by winning gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event with a Games-record score of 250.0 points. She edged compatriot Avani Lekhara by 0.4 points to secure the title, as India completed a one-two finish.Mona staged an impressive comeback in the final, climbing from sixth place to claim gold, while two-time Paralympic champion Avani settled for silver.The para-shooter continued her remarkable campaign by winning gold in the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 event on Friday. She recorded 357.5 points to set a world record, surpassing the previous mark of 356 set by Sweden's Anna Benson in July 2026.Mona contracted polio at the age of nine, affecting both her lower limbs and leaving her dependent on a wheelchair. His right arm was severed by a grass-cutting machine at his family's farm in Himachal Pradesh when he was six years old. He went on to establish himself as one of India's leading para-athletes, particularly in the high jump.With two gold medals apiece, Mona and Nishad will lead India's contingent at Saturday's closing ceremony, providing a fitting conclusion to their impressive campaigns in Aichi-Nagoya.

Article Title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The para-swimmer who won a hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games in Japan
Article Text:
Himanshu Nandal (PTI Photo)

Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
Article Summary: Himanshu Nandal completes hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026. The 22-year-old finished third in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday. Nandal is the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.

Article Title: Three medals in a day! Thulasimathi Murugesan caps Asian Para Games campaign with gold

NEW DELHI: Thulasimathi Murugesan produced a memorable triple-medal performance at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Friday, winning gold and two silver medals as India's para-badminton contingent enjoyed a productive day in Aichi-Nagoya.The 24-year-old Paris Paralympics silver medallist capped her campaign with gold in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 event, partnering Manasi Joshi to defeat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final. The Indian pair wrapped up the contest in just 28 minutes.Thulasimathi had earlier settled for silver in the women's singles SU5 final, losing 18-21, 11-21 to China's Yang. She then teamed up with Nitesh Kumar in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, but the Indian combination went down 21-11, 19-21, 14-21 to Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.Nitesh, the Paris Paralympic champion, enjoyed a successful day of his own, winning gold in the men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver with Thulasimathi.The 31-year-old defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles final."Last time I was close, I was leading 19-16 in the third set, and then I lost. So this time, winning it and again winning in two sets against Pramod is, of course, very special, and I think it's one of the rarest of the rare things to see," Nitesh said after his victory.Naveen Sivakumar added another gold for India, beating Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 in the men's singles SL4 final. Making his Asian Para Games debut, Naveen completed the win in 36 minutes.Pramod had to settle for silver after winning gold in the 2018 and 2022 editions. India's Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan also claimed silver in the women's singles SH6 final after losing to China's Li Fengmei.India continued to collect medals across disciplines on Friday. Para shooter Mona Agarwal won her second gold of the Games in the women's 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final, setting a world record with 357.5 points. She finished 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang.In para archery, Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi won gold in the men's recurve doubles event. Sandeep claimed the men's 400m T64 title, while Haney won gold in the men's javelin throw F37/38 event.India also added silver medals through Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan, Pooja Jatyan and Bhawna Choudhary in women's recurve doubles, Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46 and Nimisha Suresh in the women's long jump T47. Jehan Madan and Shubham Wadhwa secured bronze in men's doubles para table tennis MD4.India's tally stood at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with the country fourth in the standings. The contingent is chasing its best-ever Asian Para Games haul of 108 medals, achieved at Hangzhou in 2023.
Article Summary: Thulasimathi Murugesan wins gold and two silver medals at Asian Para Games 2026. Paris Paralympic silver medallist defeats China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in women's doubles final. Nitesh Kumar wins gold in men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver. India's tally stands at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with country fourth in standings.

The Indian para shooter produced a record score of 357.5 to finish 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang, setting a new World Record and Asian Para Games Record.Mona's latest triumph came after she had already struck gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event on the opening day.Mona delivered a composed performance in the 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final to secure the gold medal with a world-record score of 357.5. China's Cuiping Zhang finished second to take silver, trailing the Indian by 3.8 points.India's other finalist, Avani Lekhara , narrowly missed out on a podium finish, ending fourth. Avani had been among the leading contenders after the prone position but lost ground during the standing series, which proved decisive in the final standings.Mona had earlier teamed up with Avani for an Indian one-two finish in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event on the opening day.She won gold with a score of 250 after the seventh series, setting an Asian Para Games record and surpassing Avani's previous mark of 249.6 from the 2023 Hangzhou edition.Mona's second gold came as India continued their push to surpass their previous best performance at the Asian Para Games. At the time of reporting, India had collected 103 medals: 27 gold, 33 silver and 43 bronze and stood fourth in the overall standings, with China leading the table with 354 medals.India's record haul at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Para Games was 111 medals.

The 24-year-old, who won silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, went down 18-21, 11-21 against the Chinese shuttler at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.However, Thulasimathi's campaign is far from over, with the Indian still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events. Arsenal and Manchester City registered victories in their respective UEFA Champions League fixtures on Wednesday, while Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the campaign after going down 2-3 to Fenerbahce in their fourth-round encounter.Arsenal moved up to third in the standings following a 2-1 win over Slavia Praha, maintaining their unbeaten run in the competition. Manchester City, meanwhile, edged past RB Leipzig 3-2 at the Etihad Stadium in a closely fought contest.Liverpool's trip to Istanbul ended in disappointment as Fenerbahce scored a late winner to hand the visitors a narrow defeat.Arsenal made a strong start against Slavia Praha, with Noni Madueke opening the scoring in the ninth minute before Viktor Gyokeres doubled their advantage in the 38th minute.However, the hosts responded with a much-improved display after the break. According to Sky Sports, Slavia Praha registered 17 shots in the second half, compared to just one before the interval.Arsenal had to withstand considerable pressure, with Gabriel Magalhaes producing a crucial goal-line clearance and goalkeeper David Raya making important saves. Raya denied Oskar Kubiak before Wiktor Nowak found the net from close range in the 90th minute, setting up a tense finish.The Gunners, however, held on to secure all three points. They remain unbeaten after four matches, having collected three wins and a draw to move to 10 points, two behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain (PSG).Manchester City were made to work hard for their 3-2 victory over RB Leipzig, with Erling Haaland eventually settling the contest in the 78th minute.The hosts went ahead in the 37th minute when Castello Lukeba turned the ball into his own net. Leipzig hit back four minutes after the restart, with Ridle Baku finding the equaliser in the 49th minute after catching Gianluigi Donnarumma out at his near post.Manchester City regained the lead in the 58th minute through Enzo Fernandez, who headed home a delivery from Iliman Ndiaye. But their advantage lasted only three minutes as Antonio Nusa restored parity with a low finish into the bottom-right corner.Haaland then stepped up to deliver the decisive blow, scoring from close range in the 78th minute to seal City's third win in four matches.The Norwegian striker also extended his remarkable record against Leipzig, taking his tally to 13 goals in nine appearances against them, his highest against any single opponent. City now have nine points and occupy seventh place in the standings.Liverpool suffered their first defeat of this season's Champions League campaign after Fenerbahce came from behind twice before snatching a 3-2 victory in Istanbul.With Liverpool resting key players, including Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, their defensive vulnerabilities came to the fore against the Turkish side.The visitors took the lead through 19-year-old Trey Nyoni in the 19th minute. Fenerbahce responded 10 minutes later, with Mason Greenwood drawing the teams level in the 29th minute.Liverpool moved ahead again through Isak in the 69th minute, but Archie Brown restored parity for the hosts just four minutes later.Fenerbahce completed the turnaround in the 79th minute when Vedat Muriqi rose to meet a high cross and headed home the winning goal.The defeat left Liverpool with their first setback of the Champions League campaign. They are now eighth in the standings, one place below Manchester City.
Article Summary: Manchester City beat RB Leipzig 3-2 at the Etihad Stadium. Arsenal beat Slavia Praha 2-1 to move up to third in the Champions League standings. Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the campaign after going down 2-3 to Fenerbahce.

Article Title: From Real Madrid fan to boardroom: Rafael Nadal's journey comes full circle - 'Accepted with great excitement'

Life after tennis, but no slowing down
