Tennis legend Rafael Nadal is set to take his association with his beloved Real Madrid to a new level, with the Spanish football club offering him a place on its Board of Directors on Wednesday.The 22-time Grand Slam champion has accepted the proposal, which will now be submitted to the General Assembly of Delegate Members for ratification. Real Madrid's board agreed to put forward his appointment at its meeting on November 4. Nadal, who is already an honorary member of the club, is registered as member number 67,778.The former world No. 1 expressed his gratitude to club president Florentino Pérez and the board, describing the opportunity as a source of great excitement.“I want to thank President Florentino Pérez and the Board for proposing that I join the Board of Directors of Real Madrid. I have accepted this proposal with great excitement, a desire to learn, and a willingness to contribute everything I can,” Nadal wrote on social media, alongside a photograph of himself wearing a Real Madrid kit as a child.For the Spaniard, the appointment marks another chapter in a lifelong association with the 15-time European champions. His support for Madrid has been well known, even though his uncle Miguel Ángel Nadal represented arch-rivals Barcelona.Real Madrid described Nadal's inclusion in its boardroom as an honour, highlighting not just his achievements on the tennis court but also the qualities he displayed throughout his career.“For Real Madrid and for all madridistas, it is an immense honor that a figure of his sporting and human stature, a reference in Spanish and global sports, joins our board of directors and contributes, from this role, to the present and future of our club,” the club said in its statement.Madrid also highlighted Nadal's 92 tour-level singles titles, two Olympic gold medals, five Davis Cup triumphs with Spain and his time at the top of the world rankings. The club said his humility, respect for opponents and commitment to charity reflected its own identity.“All these values form part of Real Madrid's identity, and Rafael Nadal has embodied and championed them throughout his sporting career,” the statement added.Nadal retired from professional tennis in November 2024 after a career spanning more than two decades, during which he won a record 14 French Open titles alongside four US Open, two Wimbledon and two Australian Open crowns.However, retirement has not meant staying away from public engagements. In an interview with The Associated Press this week, Nadal spoke about fatherhood, plans involving former rival Roger Federer and an upcoming exhibition in Las Vegas.“I am traveling, I am doing stuff, I have events,” he said, explaining why he is rarely at home even after stepping away from professional tennis.His proposed appointment at Real Madrid now offers the lifelong supporter an opportunity to contribute to the club beyond the stands.
Article Summary: Real Madrid offer Rafael Nadal a place on its Board of Directors. The 22-time Grand Slam champion has accepted the proposal. Further details are expected once the clubs and the Northern League have agreed when the match can take place.Covid-related postponements were common across English football during the pandemic, when outbreaks regularly affected squads and made it difficult for clubs to meet fixture commitments. However, his plans were quickly disrupted when defender Anwar Ali was forced off with a hamstring problem in just the 18th minute, prompting the early introduction of Sandip Mandi.Still, hope rippled through the stands as Edmund Lalrindika drew a sharp save from Al-Seeb goalkeeper Ibrahil Al-Mukhaini and Bipin Singh, pouncing on the rebound, crossed it for Mohammed Rashid to miss the target from the edge of the six-yard box.But as the game wore on, East Bengal - who lost to Iraq's Al Shorta 2-3 in their previous home game - looked fatigued, sluggish and devoid of creative ideas required to get over the line.Edmund seemed to have forgotten how to score since his derby heroics in the Durand Cup final, David Lalhlansanga struggled to find his touch and with Rashid's combination with Dani Ramirez missing the usual incisiveness, East Bengal's movements in the attacking third were shorn of sparks.Habas introduced Ake Loba and Lukasz Zwolinski after the one-hour mark and Loba's first touch saw Ramirez take spectacular aim at the goal with the outside of his left boot but the Al-Seeb goalkeeper denied him with an equally eye-catching save.Thus reprieved, Al-Seeb fired an immediate warning shot, but East Bengal custodian Phurba Tempa Lachenpa kept his team's hopes alive with a stunning one-handed interception.When the visitors came calling again, the home team's luck finally ran out. Article Title: "You have no control at home": T.J. Ward’s warning to NFL wives takes Kelly Stafford’s schedule criticism to another level
Article Text:
Former Denver Broncos safety T.J. Ward has criticized Kelly Stafford after the wife of Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford questioned the NFL's scheduling system. (Instagram)

T.J. Ward questions Kelly Stafford’s public criticism

Ward says players’ wives reflect their husbands

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kelly Stafford’s complaint about the NFL schedule has drawn a sharp response from former Denver Broncos safety T.J. Ward, who believes players’ wives should be more careful about what they say publicly. Ward, a Super Bowl champion, addressed Kelly’s remarks on the “Speakeasy” podcast, arguing that a player’s spouse can influence how fans and the media view him. His comments went beyond the scheduling debate, raising questions about the balance between personal expression and a football player’s public image. Kelly’s criticism came after the Los Angeles Rams received an unusual schedule around their Week 11 bye.Kelly Stafford had raised concerns about the Rams’ schedule, saying her husband Matthew Stafford ’s team would not receive a “true bye week.” The Rams play on November 15, take their bye on November 22, and then return for a game on November 25.That leaves the team with only 10 days between games, rather than the usual 14-day gap teams get when they play on Sundays before and after a bye. Kelly, who has spent 18 years around the NFL, also highlighted the toll the schedule takes on those watching from the sidelines.“After 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season… and I have never played a single snap,” she wrote. She added, “I’m tired just watching from the stands. Can’t imagine how the guys feel.”Ward, who won a Super Bowl with Denver, took issue with her decision to share those thoughts publicly. He said, “Outside of family members, your wife is the biggest extension of you.”He then made his stance clear: “At some point, we have to tell the wives to get off Twitter. Get off. We understand your feelings; whether right or wrong, you reflect me in the biggest and most important ways. Whatever you say might as well come out of my mouth and be on my Twitter. Get the wives off of Twitter; it’s damaging.”Ward’s argument centered on how a spouse’s comments can affect a player’s reputation. He believes that when an NFL wife criticizes a team or the league, people may assume her husband shares the same view, even if he has said nothing publicly.He expanded on that point with a remark that could draw further attention: “It’s like you have no control at home,” Ward added. “She says whatever she wants; she does whatever she wants. I know that sounds crazy because, as individuals, you have that right. But if I have to watch what I say on Twitter and within the organization, then you, you watch what you say because you are a reflection of me.”The comments shift the focus from the Rams’ schedule to the expectations placed on players’ families. Ward’s view is that a public statement from a spouse can carry consequences inside the league, where players are expected to manage their own words carefully.Kelly’s complaint, however, was about the demands of the schedule and the limited recovery time it creates. The disagreement highlights a tension between an NFL player’s public image and a spouse’s right to speak openly about the league.
Article Summary: Former Denver Broncos safety T.J. Ward questions Kelly Stafford's public criticism of the NFL. Ward says players’ wives reflect their husbands. Ward: “Whatever you say might as well come out of my mouth and be on my Twitter.”

Article Title: “Troy Aikman is not like that”: Terry Bradshaw breaks silence on Cowboys legend’s reported rift with Joe Buck over $108 million ESPN deal
Article Text:

Terry Bradshaw stands up for Troy Aikman as Joe Buck contract dispute raises questions

Joe Buck's $108 million ESPN deal leaves Troy Aikman uncertain about his future

Troy Aikman and Joe Buck have spent nearly 25 years working together, but their relationship now faces questions following a reported contract dispute at ESPN. As speculation grows about a possible split, Hall of Fame quarterback Terry Bradshaw has stepped in to defend his longtime friend. He also revealed that he contacted Buck personally and does not believe money alone could explain the reported disagreement between the two broadcasters.Bradshaw's comments offer a different perspective on the controversy. While reports suggest that Buck's new $108 million contract created tension, the former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback believes Aikman is not someone who would let money damage a friendship.Bradshaw discussed the situation during an interview with FOX News host Brian Kilmeade. He revealed that he had exchanged text messages with Buck and urged him not to assume every report about the disagreement was accurate."I have talked to Buck via text and told him I don't assume everything I'm reading is correct," Bradshaw told Kilmeade.The Hall of Famer also explained why he found the reported financial disagreement difficult to believe.Both broadcasters have enjoyed successful careers, and Aikman has earned substantial money throughout his time in the NFL and broadcasting."I don't want to believe that it's the money that Buck got that's got Troy upset because Troy's making big money," Bradshaw said.He then shared what he understood about their contract negotiations. According to Bradshaw, Buck and Aikman had initially planned to approach ESPN together for new deals. However, Buck reportedly secured his extension before Aikman."I've heard that they were going to go into ESPN together and get a new deal together. Joe evidently got his before Troy. And that seems to be the rift. It's about money," he explained.Still, Bradshaw refused to believe that Aikman would allow the situation to affect their friendship."I find that hard to believe because Troy Aikman, he's not like that. And my understanding right now is things are OK," he added.However, the reported disagreement has already raised questions about what happens after the current season.Buck signed a six-year extension worth $108 million with ESPN, while Aikman continues to work under the agreement he signed in 2022. Reports suggest Aikman did not know about Buck's new deal before it became public.The situation reportedly led to an argument before the October 12, 2026, Monday Night Football broadcast between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams.Buck reportedly defended himself during their disagreement, telling Aikman, "I'm not the reason you don't have a contract."Aikman later addressed his future while speaking to reporters after the controversy surfaced. He confirmed that he would complete the season before becoming a free agent."I don't know if now is the time. I don't know if it's hard to figure out kind of what happened. I'll broadcast through this season and I'll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens," Aikman said.The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback also discussed the uncertainty during an appearance on 96.7 The Ticket Dallas."As I'm into my last year at ESPN, I'm realizing that this is something that could very well be taken away from me," Aikman said.He admitted that the situation had made him appreciate his broadcasting career even more. Aikman also expressed hope that his time in the profession was not coming to an end.The reported tension comes after the pair experienced several changes behind the scenes at ESPN. According to The Athletic, they went through five producers and directors during their first four years at the network before settling into a comfortable arrangement with Steve Ackles and Artie Kempner.For now, Buck and Aikman remain scheduled to call the 2027 Super Bowl together. They have worked alongside each other since 2002 and have called six Super Bowls as a broadcasting team.Bradshaw believes their relationship may still be on good terms. However, Aikman's next contract decision could determine whether this longtime partnership continues beyond the upcoming Super Bowl.
Article Summary: Troy Aikman and Joe Buck have spent nearly 25 years working together, but their relationship now faces questions following a reported contract dispute at ESPN. Hall of Fame quarterback Terry Bradshaw has stepped in to defend his longtime friend. Bradshaw revealed that he had exchanged text messages with Buck and urged him not to assume every report about the disagreement was accurate.
